senses.definition: (countable) A male deer, especially the male of the red deer after his fifth year.

quotes.text:
With milke-white Hartes vpon an Iuorie ſled,
Thou ſhalt be drawen amidſt the froſen Pooles,
And ſcale the yſie mountaines lofty tops:
Which with thy beautie will be soone reſolu’d.

quotes.text: We are to have hart for dinner on Jack’s birthday; you call it deer in Grenada.

quotes.text: The people of Israel knew something of hunting, as in the stories of eating hart and roebuck, and venison.
quotes.reference: 1999, James B[iser] Whisker, “Hunting in the Judaeo-Christian Tradition”, in The Right to Hunt, revised edition, Bellevue, Wash.: Merril Press, →ISBN, page 38:

quotes.text: Still, the people of Israel certainly knew about hunting, because they ate hart (red deer) and roe deer.

senses.definition: (archaic) The stag of any deer species.

quotes.text: For this reliefe much thanks, tis bitter cold, / And I am ſick at hart.
